query: According to the iteration guidelines, what should engineers do if they identify opportunities to cut scope in the planning or development lifecycle?
reference: You should always attempt to provide feedback as early as possible to product management if you can see opportunity to cut scope and deliver a smaller change no matter where you are at in the planning/development lifecycle.

query: Under what conditions is horizontal slicing preferred over vertical slicing for merge requests?
reference: Horizontal slicing works well when each part is going to be large, complex change and there is no clear way to break down the MVC further, or when each layer of the stack will be isolated and requires little to no context from the reviewers looking at the layers of the stack independently.

query: What is a sign of a possible split that can happen before work even begins on a merge request?
reference: If your issue/merge request description or comment says 'First we should do this, make sure that works, refine this', it is also a sign of a possible split that happens before work even begins.

query: If a developer needs to revert a merge request that contains a database migration, what conditions must be met, and what process should they follow to prevent the migration from executing in stable environments?
reference: First, there must be no dependencies on the change, meaning the database migration has not been run on production. Second, the developer must follow the Deployment blockers process to prevent the migration from proceeding to deploy and running on staging and production. If the migration is executed in any environment, they must communicate with the release managers in the #releases channel to discuss rolling back or turning it into a no-op.

query: What is the URL of the tool created to automate the release/feature determination workflow?
reference: The tool can be found here: https://gitlab.com/darbyfrey/releasepost.

query: In the release/feature determination workflow, what condition must all related merge requests meet to consider the feature complete?
reference: All related MRs assigned to the current milestone should be merged in order to be included in the release. If there are any MRs assigned to the current milestone that are not merged it should be determined that the feature is not complete.

query: How can an Engineering Manager verify that merged merge requests have been deployed and are running in production?
reference: This can be done by querying chatops with the sha of the merge commit.

query: What is the deadline (day of the month) by which release post MRs must be merged?
reference: The release post MRs must be merged by the 17th of the month. In order to accommodate that timeline a EMs should evaluate release post MRs when they are ready and merge them early if possible.

query: If a feature is not considered complete because a related merge request is not merged by the 17th of the month, what action should the EM take regarding the release post MR, and how does this affect the next milestone cycle start date?
reference: If a feature is not complete, the EM should update the milestone on the release post MR to be the milestone of the next release. After the 17th of the month, any release post MRs not merged should be moved to the next milestone. The next milestone begins the Saturday after the code cut-off, which is the Friday prior to the release date (the third Thursday of the release month).

query: What is the stakeholders' priority order when values compete in a merge request review?
reference: Users > contributors > ourselves

query: According to the reviewer values, what should a reviewer do if they notice that all they have pointed out in a review are nitpicks?
reference: If you, as a reviewer, notice that all you have pointed out are nitpicks, consider approving (and merging) without adding an additional review cycle.

query: How does the trainee maintainer review feedback process differ for general backend reviews compared to the CI/CD components project, and which Slack channels are notified upon approval for each?
reference: For general backend reviews, the reviewer summarizes why they believe the MR is ready to be merged, and the maintainer responds with a 👍 if they agree. Upon approval, the change is announced in `#backend_maintainers` and `#backend`. For CI/CD components, the trainee creates a merge request citing components they developed, assigns it to their manager, pings `@gitlab-org/maintainers/ci-components` for review, gets at least 2 approvals from existing maintainers, and upon approval is announced in the `#ci_components_maintainers` channel.

query: How are the quality expectations for legacy code compared to green-field code in merge reviews?
reference: If the author is working on legacy code we shouldn't have as high-quality expectations as green-field code. The changes should still lead to a net gain in code quality, though.

query: What are the negative costs associated with nitpicks in code reviews?
reference: They create needless MR cycles (explicitly or implicitly), they create cognitive load, and they can possibly damage the contributor's morale.

query: According to the reviewer values and team guidelines, who ultimately owns and upholds the requirements of a merge request, and how should a team coordinate frontend and backend changes to ensure independent delivery?
reference: Product/UX ultimately owns and upholds the requirements of a merge request. To ensure independent delivery, the team should separate the frontend and backend code into separate MRs and merge them independently under feature flags. A separate MR containing the integration and removal of the feature flags should only be merged when both the frontend and backend MRs are on the master branch.

query: Name at least three engineering processes listed under the Links section of the related workflows index.
reference: Feature Change Lock (FCL), Production Change Lock (PCL), Error budgets, Capacity planning, Rapid actions, Working groups, InfraDev, Cross Functional Prioritization, Incident Review, Production readiness reviews, and Deployment Processes.

query: What is the expected maintainership completion timeframe for a newly hired Senior+ engineer?
reference: Newly hired Senior+: During onboarding, newly hired senior+ engineers will be asked to become trainee maintainers instead of reviewers. We expect their maintainership to be complete within 12 months of their onboarding completion.

query: What specific criteria must a wider community member meet to qualify as a Leading Organization, and what is the review-response SLO time frame for their merge requests compared to standard team members?
reference: When an organization or individual without affiliations reaches 20 merged merge requests or more within the last 3 completed months, they qualify as a Leading Organization. Merge requests from authors of Leading Organizations receive a Review-response SLO of less than 4 business days, whereas requests from GitLab team members have an SLO of less than 2 business days.

query: What is the formula and target SLO for a review response to a GitLab team member?
reference: Review-response SLO = (time when review is provided) - (time MR is assigned to reviewer). For GitLab team members, the SLO is less than 2 business days.

query: What is the target review response SLO for authors from Leading Organizations?
reference: From authors of Leading Organizations: Review-response SLO < 4 business days.

query: What should a reviewer do if they realize they cannot review a merge request within the Review-response SLO timeframe?
reference: If you don't think you can review a merge request in the Review-response SLO time frame, let the author know as soon as possible in the comments (no later than 36 hours after first receiving the review request) and try to help them find another reviewer or maintainer who is able to, so that they can be unblocked and get on with their work quickly. Remove yourself as a reviewer.

query: What are the two ways team members can qualify as domain experts?
reference: Implicit (e.g. team members working in a specific stage/group or on a specific feature) and Self-identification.

query: To whom is the ability to accept (merge) merge requests restricted?
reference: Note that while all engineers can review all merge requests, the ability to accept merge requests is restricted to maintainers.

query: What is the target ratio of engineers to maintainers that GitLab aims to keep?
reference: We aim to keep the engineer : maintainer ratio under 6, for both frontend and backend.

query: For a broken master incident, what is the triage phase service level objective (SLO), and how does the escalation timeline handle untriaged, recurring incidents before they reach dev-escalation?
reference: The triage phase SLO is 4 hours from the 2nd occurrence of a broken master incident creation until assignment. For recurring incidents, if there is no triage activity, the system pings the attributed group's Slack channel after 10 minutes and 30 minutes of inactivity, pings the stage channel after 3 hours and 40 minutes of inactivity, and finally escalates to dev-escalation after 4 hours of inactivity.
